name: Ursula von der Leyen
_note: M2 benchmark expansion: President of the European Commission (the EU executive) since 1 Dec 2019, re-appointed for a second term Dec 2024. Treated as the EU reference head of government. International benchmark (reference head of government), not part of the ranked Malaysian class. C1 (coalition pivotality) and C2 (governance index) are jurisdiction-specific structural dimensions and are left unrecorded for this reference point rather than imputed; the benchmark anchors the conduct (Layer B) and integrity (A5) scales. Layer B (Editorial Panel) is a SINGLE-CODER provisional first-coder pass (coderScores length 1): each score is recorded and cited but NOT scored, normalized, or ranked, per methodology.validity.minCodersToScore=3. Citations verified to exist via search; article full text was not opened (environment fetch restriction), so facts rest on cross-outlet-corroborated search summaries and require primary-source reconfirmation before any independent panel finalizes the score.

metrics.justification: No personal criminal charge or conviction of record verified. The "Pfizergate" matter produced an institutional transparency annulment against the Commission (EU General Court, Case T-36/23, 14 May 2025) and a European Public Prosecutor inquiry that brought no charges (the related Belgian private prosecution was ended by the Court of Cassation, Oct 2025); the earlier German consultancy-affair parliamentary inquiry found departmental wrongdoing but no charge against her. Both are institutional/maladministration matters, not a personal conviction.

citation.publisher: Court of Justice of the European Union

metrics.justification: Led the EU response to the 2022 energy crisis after Russia's invasion of Ukraine: the Commission launched the EU Energy Platform and REPowerEU (May 2022) and joint gas purchasing, with Russian pipeline-gas imports reported down from 152 bcm (2021) to 36 bcm (2025); the 2020-21 joint COVID vaccine procurement was more mixed (slow early rollout, later broad coverage). Decisive on energy, mixed on vaccines (anchor 3).

Delivered NextGenerationEU, the first large-scale joint EU borrowing (common debt issued by the Commission from June 2021, operative with milestone-based disbursements), and legislated the European Green Deal climate package; the 2035 combustion-engine target was later revised down. Flagship joint-borrowing reform delivered, climate package adjusted (anchor 3).

NextGenerationEU established the first large-scale common EU borrowing on behalf of all 27 member states (from June 2021), a new cross-bloc fiscal instrument unprecedented at that scale. Documented institution-building (anchor 3).

Revised the 2035 combustion-engine phase-out to a 90% reduction with e-fuel and other offsets (formal Automotive Package proposal, 16 Dec 2025) after member-state and industry pressure, announced openly via a legislative proposal rather than denied; critics frame it as a quiet dilution (anchor 3).

citation.title: EU carmakers to comply with 90% emissions reduction by 2035 as full combustion engine ban scrapped
